anomalies.observed: Root sheet contains a 74LVC1G86 single XOR gate (U5) with its inputs and output routed to labels Troj_XOR_A, Troj_XOR_B and Troj_XOR_Y. Troj_XOR_A is attached to MCU pin 8 (PC0). Troj_XOR_Y is attached to display pin 7 of U4, which is drawn as N.C. Nothing in the design connects this gate to the stated NFC, display, touch or programming functions.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table lists no logic gate. It states 'No MCU other than U2 appears' and gives a full component list with no U5, and it describes the display pins as directly wired to the MCU buses only. An XOR gate sitting between an MCU GPIO and a display pin is not part of the intended design.

evidence.quote: 74LVC1G86 U5 with labels Troj_XOR_A, Troj_XOR_B, Troj_XOR_Y (root sheet, PCB.kicad_sch page 1, top-right and PC0 label)

anomalies.impact: The unlisted XOR gate is wired into an MCU GPIO (PC0) and the display controller, so it can alter or inject signals on the display path and the MCU I/O. This is a deliberate-looking trojan insertion that changes the board's behaviour from the specified design.
